uncertainty: Ten distinct pinned Java Maven package paths passed one valid local HTTP/1.1 GET request control and exposed the request method, target, version, Host, and X-Parsarium headers. These are ten verified package paths, not ten independent engines: Netty 3, 4, and 5 share project ancestry, while httpcore and httpcore5 are two Apache HttpComponents Core major branches. Netty 5 is an alpha release and is labeled as such. The working goal of 20 has not been met; ten paths remain. Five Maven Central queries were bounded at 100 hits each. The broad http1 and HTTP/1.1 queries each reported 7,858 total and saved the first 100 identical, mostly unrelated HTTP package hits, giving 200 saved hits but only 100 unique; http parser, http request parser, and http codec timed out in the latest snapshot, so they provide no absence evidence. Targeted Maven releases and official API documentation supplied the ten verified paths, including NanoHTTPD's documented protected local-stream session API. Three plausible leads remain unresolved: Grizzly, Snice, and a historical WebPieces artifact. Other search hits have not all been reviewed, and the most-used top 20 is unknown. NanoHTTPD exposes the parsed method, target and headers through a local session callback, but its public session interface does not expose the protocol version; its adapter omits that field. The single ordinary request only establishes the observed format-aware behavior for that control. Java SE 25 public APIs reviewed expose network HTTP clients or servers, not a documented local raw message parser. No vulnerability, malformed-input, or resource-use experiments were run.
